front: Au secours !
back: Help!
context: The cry for help. Also: 'À l'aide !'

front: Appelez une ambulance, vite !
back: Call an ambulance, quickly!
context: In France the SAMU (medical emergencies) is 15; 112 works everywhere in Europe.

front: Il faut appeler les pompiers.
back: We need to call the fire brigade.
context: Firefighters (18) also handle many medical emergencies in France.

front: Quel est le numéro de la police ?
pronunciation: [kel eh luh nü-may-roh duh lah poh-LEES]
back: What's the number for the police?
context: 17 for the police in France; 112 is the European emergency number.

front: Il y a eu un accident sur l'autoroute.
pronunciation: [eel yah ü an nak-see-DAHN sür loh-toh-ROOT]
back: There's been an accident on the motorway.
context: 'Il y a eu' = passé composé of 'il y a'.

front: Est-ce que quelqu'un est blessé ?
back: Is anyone injured?
context: 'Blessé' = injured. False friend: not 'blessed' (béni).

front: Il a perdu connaissance.
back: He's lost consciousness.
context: 'Perdre connaissance' = to faint, pass out. Also 's'évanouir'.

front: Elle ne respire plus !
back: She's not breathing!
context: 'Respirer' = to breathe.

front: Ne bougez pas, les secours arrivent.
back: Don't move, help is on the way.
context: 'Les secours' = emergency services.

front: Restez calme et suivez les consignes.
back: Stay calm and follow the instructions.
context: 'Les consignes' = instructions (safety).

front: On m'a volé mon sac.
back: My bag has been stolen.
context: 'On m'a volé' (someone stole from me) is how French usually says this. 'Un vol' = theft.

front: Je voudrais porter plainte.
back: I'd like to file a complaint.
context: 'Porter plainte' = to report a crime to the police.

front: Je dois déclarer la perte de mon passeport.
pronunciation: [zhuh dwah day-klah-ray lah pehrt duh mohn pas-POR]
back: I need to report the loss of my passport.
context: 'Une déclaration de perte' at the police station; then contact your embassy.

front: Où est le commissariat le plus proche ?
pronunciation: [oo eh luh koh-mee-sar-YAH luh plü PROSH]
back: Where's the nearest police station?
context: 'Le commissariat' (city police) or 'la gendarmerie' (rural).

front: J'ai été témoin de l'accident.
back: I witnessed the accident.
context: 'Un témoin' = a witness.

front: Au feu !
back: Fire!
context: The alarm cry for a fire.

front: Sortez immédiatement du bâtiment.
back: Leave the building immediately.
context: 'Sortir de' = to get out of.

front: Il y a une fuite de gaz.
back: There's a gas leak.
context: 'Une fuite' = leak. 'Une fuite d'eau' = a water leak.

front: Ne prenez pas l'ascenseur en cas d'incendie.
pronunciation: [nuh pruh-nay pah lah-sahn-SUHR ahn kah dan-sahn-DEE]
back: Do not use the elevator in case of fire.
context: 'En cas de' = in case of. 'Un incendie' = a fire (building, forest).

front: Je me suis fait agresser dans la rue.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh swee feh tah-greh-SAY dahn lah RÜ]
back: I was attacked in the street.
context: 'Se faire' + infinitive = to have something done to you.

front: Pouvez-vous décrire la personne ?
back: Can you describe the person?
context: 'Décrire' = to describe.

front: Il était grand, brun, et il portait une veste noire.
pronunciation: [ee lay-teh GRAHN, BRAN, ay eel por-teh tün vest NWAHR]
back: He was tall, dark-haired, and wearing a black jacket.
context: Imparfait for descriptions in the past.

front: Ma voiture est tombée en panne.
back: My car broke down.
context: 'Tomber en panne' = to break down. 'Une dépanneuse' = tow truck.

front: J'ai crevé un pneu.
back: I got a flat tire.
context: 'Crever' = to puncture (also 'to die', of animals, and 'to be exhausted').

front: Il faut mettre le gilet jaune et le triangle.
pronunciation: [eel foh meh-truh luh zhee-leh ZHOHN ay luh tree-YAHN-gluh]
back: You have to put on the yellow vest and set up the warning triangle.
context: Mandatory in French cars.

front: Mon enfant a disparu, je ne le trouve plus !
pronunciation: [mohn nahn-fahn ah dees-pah-RÜ, zhuh nuh luh troov PLÜ]
back: My child has gone missing, I can't find him!
context: 'Disparaître' → disparu.

front: Je suis bloqué dans l'ascenseur.
back: I'm stuck in the elevator.
context: 'Être bloqué' = to be stuck.

front: La rue est barrée à cause d'une manifestation.
pronunciation: [lah rü eh bah-RAY ah kohz dün mah-nee-fes-tah-SYOHN]
back: The street is closed because of a demonstration.
context: 'Barré' = closed off. 'Une manifestation' / 'une manif' = demonstration.

front: Attention, ça glisse !
back: Careful, it's slippery!
context: 'Glisser' = to slip, slide.

front: Il y a un risque d'inondation dans la région.
pronunciation: [eel yah an reesk dee-nohn-dah-SYOHN dahn lah ray-ZHYOHN]
back: There's a risk of flooding in the region.
context: 'Une inondation' = flood.

front: Une alerte orange aux orages a été déclenchée.
pronunciation: [ün ah-lehrt oh-RAHNZH oh zoh-RAZH ah ay-tay day-klahn-SHAY]
back: An orange storm warning has been issued.
context: Météo-France uses color-coded alerts: jaune, orange, rouge.

front: Gardez votre sang-froid.
back: Keep your cool.
context: 'Le sang-froid' (cold blood) = composure.

front: J'ai besoin d'un médecin qui parle anglais.
pronunciation: [zhay buh-zwan dan mayd-SAN kee parl ahn-GLEH]
back: I need a doctor who speaks English.
context: 'Qui' + verb: a doctor who speaks.

front: Mon assurance couvre les frais médicaux ?
back: Does my insurance cover medical costs?
context: 'Couvrir' = to cover. 'Médical' → médicaux in the plural.

front: Heureusement, il y a eu plus de peur que de mal.
pronunciation: [uh-ruhz-MAHN, eel yah ü plü duh PUHR kuh duh MAHL]
back: Fortunately, it was more of a scare than anything.
context: Idiom: more fear than harm, no real damage.
